t:
The Act entitled “An Act Authorizing the Commissioners of the District of Columbia to make regulations respecting the rights and privileges of the fish wharf”, approved March 19, 1906 (sec. 37–205.01, D.C. Official Code), is amended—
    (1) by striking “operate as a municipal fish wharf and market” and inserting “operate as a market and for such other uses as the Mayor determines to be appropriate”; 
    (2) by striking “, and said wharf shall constitute the sole wharf for the landing of fish and oysters for sale in the District of Columbia”; and 
    (3) by striking “operation of said municipal fish wharf and market” and inserting “operation of said market”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the phrase "make regulations" in the amended Act's title, or the Mayor's discretion over uses, signals rulemaking or outside consultation. But the title is only a proper-noun reference, and the section simply edits text to broaden the permitted uses of the wharf and remove its exclusive fish-landing status. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: operate as a market and for such other uses as the Mayor determines to be appropriate

qwen_block.w: This section amends a statute to change the authorized uses of a fish wharf and grants the Mayor of the District of Columbia discretion to determine appropriate uses. It does not require consultation with, or participation by, any outside parties (such as the public, states, or private entities) in making that decision. The Mayor is a government official, and the text describes internal administrative authority rather than a participatory process.
qwen_block.s: The Act entitled “An Act Authorizing the Commissioners of the District of Columbia to make regulations respecting the rights and privileges of the fish wharf”, approved March 19, 1906 (sec. 37–205.01, D.C. Official Code), is amended— (1) by striking “operate as a municipal fish wharf and market” and inserting “operate as a market and for such other uses as the Mayor determines to be appropriate”; (2) by striking “, and said wharf shall constitute the sole wharf for the landing of fish and oysters for sale in the District of Columbia”; and (3) by striking “operation of said municipal fish wharf and market” and inserting “operation of said market”.

opus.w: This section changes the wording of an existing D.C. law about the fish wharf. It adds no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue. The tempting reading treats the Mayor's power to decide uses, or the title's mention of 'regulations', as participation. But the Mayor is the decision-maker, not an outside party being consulted before a federal decision. This section also creates no new rulemaking authority.
opus.s: by striking “operate as a municipal fish wharf and market” and inserting “operate as a market and for such other uses as the Mayor determines to be appropriate”
opus.b:
1. **The tempting reading:** The amended statute is an Act "Authorizing the Commissioners of the District of Columbia to make regulations." That looks like a grant of rulemaking power, and the new text lets "the Mayor" decide what the wharf can be used for. Under Example 6, granting regulatory authority can count as participation.
2. **Why it fails:** This section only rewrites the wording of an existing law. It creates no new rulemaking power, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or consultation. The Mayor is the one making the decision, not an outside party being consulted before a federal decision. The regulation-making authority comes from the original 1906 Act, which this section doesn't create.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a statute to grant the Mayor of the District of Columbia the authority to determine appropriate uses for a fish wharf. It does not require the Mayor to consult with the public, state/local governments, or other outside entities before making this determination. The decision is unilateral and administrative, lacking any mechanism for external participation such as public hearings, advisory committees with non-federal members, or required consultations.
qwen_chat.s: operate as a market and for such other uses as the Mayor determines to be appropriate
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Mayor determining "appropriate uses" involves public input or consultation. However, the text itself does not mandate any such consultation; it simply grants discretion to the Mayor. Furthermore, the District of Columbia government is generally considered part of the local government structure, but even if viewed as federal, the decision-making process described is unilateral by the Mayor without any required external participation.
